# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_SET_LIMIT::response_t, src/rpc/core_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:1894-1904
#         { limit_up int64_t, limit_down int64_t } -- SIGNED, unlike get_limit's uint64_t
#         (:1867-1868). See get_limit.json.
# base:   rpc_response_base only (status, untrusted) :101-112
# request: { limit_down int64_t, limit_up int64_t } (:1883-1889), kB/s, `-1` resets to the default
#         and `0` means "leave unchanged" (DESIGN.md §1b.3).
# The response ECHOES the limits in force after the change, which is what §5c's `node limit`
#         payload renders as limit_up_kbps / limit_down_kbps with changed: true.
# THIS FIXTURE IS STATIC, so it echoes one fixed pair (the `--up 1024` of DESIGN.md §8's gate
#         commands, with limit_down left at get_limit.json's 8192). fmonero-mock is stateless by
#         design (DESIGN.md §8 Phase 0), so it cannot echo back whatever the request asked for; a
#         test that needs the echo to match its own argument asserts on the RECORDED REQUEST in the
#         --log file, not on this response.
# ERROR CHANNEL: a bad parameter comes back as HTTP 200 with `status: "Invalid parameter"` and no
#         JSON-RPC error object (DESIGN.md §1b.3) -- reachable from the mock with
#         `--fail set_limit=0:'Invalid parameter'`, which on a legacy endpoint sets `status` rather
#         than producing a JSON-RPC error.
# gate:   MAP_URI_AUTO_JON2("/set_limit", ..., !m_restricted) (src/rpc/core_rpc_server.h:136) ->
#         HTTP 404 on a restricted node, not -32601.
# One of the four files DESIGN.md §8 Phase 0 names as "without which `node limit --up 1024` is an
# AMBER row with no response to serve".
